headline: Hacktron researchers pointed Claude at OpenAI's sign-in flow and reached internal code, on the same day one plugin flaw surfaced in all four major AI coding agents.

emerging_trends.text: Plugin4Shell, hardcoded credentials sitting in 12 percent of public MCP configuration files, and prompt injection that drains AWS AgentCore Harness credentials all point at one soft spot, the plumbing developers bolt onto AI agents.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Plugin4Shell Opens Four AI Coding Agents

emerging_trends.text: One stolen API key now reaches everything downstream, as the Brevo intruders showed when they turned a single Cloudflare credential into ClickFix scripts running on 100,000 websites.

Malware authors increasingly hand the keyboard to a model, with PhantomRaven's verbose comments and placeholder blocks betraying a large language model and RatHat shipping an AI subsystem that drives stolen Android phones.

topics.title: Plugin4Shell Opens Four AI Coding Agents
topics.latest_developments: Air Security disclosed on September 18, 2026 that Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI share one zero-click remote code execution flaw it calls Plugin4Shell, the first supply-chain vulnerability of the AI agent ecosystem: whoever controls a plugin's source repository swaps the code an agent installs even when the agent pins that plugin to a specific reviewed version. Anthropic fixed it in Claude Code 2.1.179 and OpenAI in Codex 0.146.0, and GitHub Copilot and Gemini CLI still carry it.
topics.summary: Anyone whose coding agent installs plugins from a marketplace is exposed, and a successful attacker gains the same access to company systems and data as the employee running the agent. Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 separately showed that default settings in Amazon's AgentCore Harness let prompt injection pull credentials out, and Hush Security found hardcoded API keys and access tokens in 12 percent of credential slots across roughly 82,000 public MCP configuration files on GitHub.

sources.title: Zero-click RCE vulnerability hit four major AI coding agents, two remain unpatched
Plugin4Shell Lets Repository Owners Swap Pinned Plugin Code Across Four AI Coding Agents
A Vault with a Heap-View: The Uncomfortable Space Between AgentCore Harness and Identity

topics.title: Check Point Management Servers Yield Root
topics.latest_developments: Check Point Software shipped a fix through its LivePatch channel for a critical flaw that lets an attacker with no credentials run code as root over the network on Security Management and Log Servers, and says it sees no sign of exploitation; Kaspersky and Tanium patched product flaws the same day, and Microsoft closed 18 vulnerabilities across Azure and its AI-branded products, among them CVE-2026-85889, a 10.0-rated missing authentication for a critical function in Azure AI Foundry that hands an unauthorized attacker elevated privileges over a network and that Microsoft fixed with no customer action required.
topics.summary: The Security Management Server controls firewall policy and administrator access, so root on that box hands an intruder the rules governing every gateway it manages. Check Point customers should take the LivePatch update immediately.

sources.title: New Check Point flaw lets hackers execute code with root privileges
Critical Check Point Management Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code as Root
Check Point, Kaspersky, Tanium Patch Product Vulnerabilities
Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation

topics.title: Hacktron Uses Claude to Reach OpenAI Employee Accounts
topics.latest_developments: Researchers at Hacktron used Claude to build a working exploit, chained it with a flaw in OpenAI's sign-in flow, and reached OpenAI employee accounts and sensitive internal GitHub data, and OpenAI paid them a bug bounty for the demonstration.
topics.summary: The work shows a frontier model carrying the offensive engineering, from finding the weakness to writing the exploit, against the company that builds a competing frontier model. Every organization that relies on a single sign-on path into its source code should assume attackers now run the same loop.

sources.title: Researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI
AI-Built Exploit and Sign-In Flaw Opened Path to Internal OpenAI Code

topics.title: Brevo Attack Reaches 100,000 Websites
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek put the count at 100,000 websites on September 18, 2026, and detailed the method: the attackers used the stolen Cloudflare API key to deploy a Cloudflare worker that injected the malicious scripts, a day after Brevo confirmed the theft.
topics.summary: Brevo, the French email marketing platform, lost a Cloudflare API key that attackers turned into ClickFix scripts running on its own sites and inside the JavaScript files its customers embed on theirs, making every one of those sites a malware distribution point. Site owners who load Brevo JavaScript should audit their pages and rotate anything the injected scripts could have touched.

sources.title: Brevo Supply Chain Attack Injects Malware Into 100,000 Websites
Brevo supply-chain attack injected ClickFix scripts on customer sites

topics.title: Attackers Exploit Orkes Conductor as Docker Sandboxes Leak macOS Hosts
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported on September 18, 2026 that attackers exploit CVE-2026-58138 in Orkes Conductor, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw they reach through inline workflow definitions, and Docker warned in a September 15 announcement that CVE-2026-77179, rated critical, lets malicious code inside a Docker Sandboxes virtual machine on macOS escape the shared project directory and read or change any file on the host.
topics.summary: Orkes Conductor orchestrates microservice workflows, and the flaw gives an unauthenticated caller code execution on the orchestrator. The Docker escape runs with the rights of the host account that started the virtual machine, collapsing the isolation developers rely on when they run untrusted code.

sources.title: Critical Orkes Conductor Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
Critical Docker Sandboxes Flaw Lets Malicious Guest Code Read and Modify macOS Host Files

topics.title: LLM-Written Stealers Ride npm Packages
topics.latest_developments: Researchers at OpenSourceMalware identified 13 npm packages delivering WeaselBiscuit, a previously undocumented JavaScript stealer that harvests Chrome extension storage and overlaps functionally with BeaverTail and a second strain from North Korea's Contagious Interview campaign; separately, analysts tied a financially motivated actor claiming to be a bug bounty hunter to the PhantomRaven stealer on npm and judged with high confidence that a large language model wrote it, citing verbose comments, placeholder code, and token-analysis patterns.
topics.summary: Both families reach developers through the npm registry and take browser-held credentials and wallet data off the machines that build software. Development teams should pin dependencies, audit recently added packages, and treat Chrome extension storage as credential material.

sources.title: WeaselBiscuit Stealer Spreads via 13 npm Packages to Harvest Chrome Extension Storage
Claimed Bug Bounty Hunter Likely Used LLM to Build PhantomRaven npm Stealer

topics.title: RatHat Android Trojan Drives Phones With AI
topics.latest_developments: Researchers flagged RatHat on September 17, 2026, Android malware that China-based operators spread through targeted smishing and malvertising to deceptive third-party download portals, which carries an AI-powered subsystem that navigates and controls a compromised handset and abuses the Android Debug Bridge to keep shell access after the victim uninstalls the app.
topics.summary: The AI layer lets one operator work many phones at once without hand-driving each screen, and the ADB persistence survives the obvious remedy. Android users should install only from Google Play and check developer options for enabled debugging.

sources.title: RatHat Android Malware Abuses ADB to Retain Shell Access After Uninstall
New RatHat Android malware uses AI to automate device control

topics.title: Abandoned Apps and a Resurrected CDN Domain
topics.latest_developments: Researchers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst analyzed 61,500 abandoned Android smart home and internet-of-things companion apps drawn from the AndroZoo archive and found nearly three in four carrying software dependencies with documented vulnerabilities, while The Hacker News traced a domain that once served a wound-down content delivery network: the owner let it expire, someone re-registered it in July 2025, and thousands of websites, code repositories, and documentation pages still hard-code hostnames beneath it.
topics.summary: Millions of people still run companion apps for smart plugs, cameras, and thermostats that stopped receiving updates years ago, and those apps keep sending data to servers nobody maintains. Whoever controls a re-registered CDN domain can answer every one of those stale requests with code of their own choosing, so teams should grep their repositories and pages for third-party hostnames and verify who owns each one today.

sources.title: Abandoned IoT apps keep sending sensitive data to broken servers
An Abandoned CDN Domain Was Re-Registered. Thousands of Sites Still Call It.

topics.title: SynthID Watermarking Erodes Model Refusals
topics.latest_developments: Researchers found that turning on SynthID text watermarking changes how large language models answer harmful prompts, and the watermarking can push a model to follow instructions it would otherwise refuse.
topics.summary: Watermarking exists to mark machine-generated text for provenance, and this work shows the same mechanism shifting the token choices that safety training depends on. Anyone deploying watermarked models should re-run refusal testing with the watermark enabled.

sources.title: LLMs respond differently to harmful prompts when AI watermarking is used
Are AIs Still Struggling with CAPTCHAs?

topics.title: CISA Retires Its Weekly Vulnerability Bulletin
topics.latest_developments: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency ended its weekly vulnerability summary, the long-running roundup of newly published flaws, following Binding Operational Directive 26-04, which orders federal agencies to rank vulnerabilities by real-world risk instead of working down a list by severity score.
topics.summary: Federal agencies and the many private teams that read the bulletin lose a standing catalog of new CVEs and gain a mandate to prioritize what attackers actually exploit. Security teams that built processes around the weekly summary should shift to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and exploitation telemetry.

sources.title: CISA Retires Weekly Vulnerability Bulletin in Risk-Based Pivot
CISA Ditches Weekly Vulnerability Roundups for Risk-Based Focus

business_politics.title: Turkey Moves to Liquidate Funds in a Ponzi Inquiry
business_politics.latest_developments: The Financial Times reported Friday, September 18, that Turkish authorities have moved to liquidate the investment funds at the center of what regulators describe as a Ponzi-like scheme, forcing big Turkish banks to sell the assets held inside them.
business_politics.summary: Roughly 300,000 investors hold positions in the funds, and the unwinding comes amid fears that the assets carried inflated valuations. A Financial Times column the same day told U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to watch the affair, arguing that stretched markets break without any fraud at all.

business_politics.title: The Bank of Japan Lifts Rates to 1.25%
business_politics.latest_developments: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate to 1.25% Friday, September 18, the highest since 1995, and said it will hold to a quarterly pace of tightening.
business_politics.summary: The yen fell 1.2% to a two-week low of 158.05 per dollar after two board members signaled that future increases may come more slowly than markets had priced. Higher yields at home give Tokyo investors, long among the largest buyers of U.S. Treasurys, a reason to keep money in Japan.

business_politics.title: Buffett Hands the Berkshire Chair to His Son
business_politics.latest_developments: Berkshire Hathaway said Friday morning, September 18, that Warren Buffett will step down as chairman and that his son Howard Buffett will succeed him.
business_politics.summary: Warren Buffett led the $1 trillion conglomerate for more than six decades and takes the title of chair emeritus. Howard Buffett, long designated to protect the culture of the company, inherits the chairmanship of an insurer, railroad, and utility owner whose paper holdings move markets.

business_politics.title: Russia Seizes Nestlé's Local Operations
business_politics.latest_developments: A presidential decree reported Friday, September 18, put the Russian businesses of Nestlé and the French retailers Auchan and Leroy Merlin under temporary external administration.
business_politics.summary: Moscow stripped operational control from three Western companies that kept trading in Russia after the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, and Nestlé is weighing its options for the unit. The seizures raise the cost of remaining for every multinational still holding Russian assets.

sources.title: Russia Seizes Control of Nestlé’s Local Operations

business_politics.title: Oil Slides Below $100
business_politics.latest_developments: Crude fell for a third straight session Friday, September 18, with West Texas Intermediate dropping under $100 a barrel and Brent near $102.
business_politics.summary: Traders are betting Saudi Arabia will restore export capacity after drone damage shut its East-West pipeline, which eased the supply fear that drove diesel to a record $6.27 a gallon this month. Gold climbed above $4,400 an ounce, Treasury yields eased, and U.S. stock futures rose as AI shares extended Thursday's rally.

business.title: A Second Superload Rolls Next Week
business.latest_developments: WPXI reported Friday, September 18, that a second slow-moving superload will cross Armstrong, Indiana, and Westmoreland counties next week, following the 380-ton first haul that crawled through Delmont on Wednesday, September 16.
business.summary: Escort vehicles, the Pennsylvania State Police, and bucket trucks that lift wires out of the way will run ahead of and behind the truck, which carries equipment to data center construction near Homer City in Indiana County. The Pennsylvania Department of Transportation warns drivers that the haul will occupy two lanes at times and move as a rolling slowdown, with roughly 50 more superloads scheduled over the next four months.

business.title: The Canada Trade War Reaches Pennsylvania's Shop Floors
business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Friday, September 18, that the escalating tariff fight with Canada is hitting Pennsylvania's largest export market and the manufacturers that sell into it.
business.summary: Christian Klanica, who runs a machining company in Hempfield, Westmoreland County, said the levies flying between Washington and Ottawa change so often that he can no longer keep track of which ones apply to his work. Canada buys more Pennsylvania goods than any other country, which puts the state's machine shops and metal fabricators at the center of the dispute.

sources.title: ‘So much chaos’: Escalating trade war with Canada impacts Pa.’s largest export market

business.title: Butterwood Sells Dessert After Dark
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper's food column made the case Friday, September 18, for Butterwood as the city's answer to a late-night sweet tooth.
business.summary: Bakeries run on 4 a.m. shifts, and the column argues Butterwood inverts that schedule by keeping its counter going for customers who want cake at night. The piece lands as Pittsburgh's after-dark dining options draw fresh attention.

sources.title: Satisfying a late-night sweet tooth at Butterwood

around_town.title: County Rules Raise North Allegheny's Pool Costs
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Friday, September 18, that Allegheny County requirements have pushed up the cost of the North Allegheny School District's natatorium renovation, according to a presentation the district gave at its September 9 school board meeting.
around_town.summary: The district, which serves McCandless, Marshall, Bradford Woods, and Franklin Park, is weighing alternative versions of the project as the price climbs. The board must decide how much of the swimming facility work to keep before it commits the money.

sources.title: North Allegheny renovation update includes cost increases, project alternatives

around_town.title: A Dry Saturday, a Wet Sunday
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE called Sunday, September 20, an Impact Day in its Friday morning outlook, September 18, with rain arriving Saturday night after a dry start to the weekend.
around_town.summary: The Post-Gazette reported the same morning that repeated heavy downpours have flooded Western Pennsylvania through a stretch of weeks that gives residents little time to clean up between storms. Elizabeth Township took 2 inches in under 90 minutes Thursday, and Oakmont is still working through damage from a storm three weeks ago.

around_town.title: Bracken House Tenants Hear About the Garage
around_town.latest_developments: The Bracken House apartment complex on Pittsburgh's North Shore held a town hall Thursday night, September 17, to update residents on its collapsed parking garage.
around_town.summary: Tenants have gone without their parking structure since it gave way, and WTAE reported frustration among residents waiting for a timeline and a repair plan. The building sits within walking distance of Acrisure Stadium and PNC Park, where game-day parking already runs tight.

around_town.title: Westmoreland Widens Its Lead Pipe Removal
around_town.latest_developments: The Municipal Authority of Westmoreland County plans a substantial expansion of its lead service line replacement program, TribLive reported Friday, September 18.
around_town.summary: The authority supplies water across Westmoreland County and has been pulling lead pipes out of its distribution system under federal replacement requirements. The expansion widens the number of homes whose service lines the authority will dig up and replace.

events.latest_developments: The Pittsburgh International Jazz Festival runs its final two days downtown through Sunday, September 20, and the Post-Gazette profiled 103-year-old retired judge Warren Watson, who has kept the city's jazz tradition going.
events.summary: The 16th edition of the festival fills downtown Pittsburgh from Thursday, September 17, through Sunday, September 20, with Grammy winners Samara Joy and Lalah Hathaway on the bill. events.summary: Fall Fest runs through Sunday, November 1, at Soergel Orchards, beside the northbound Wexford exit of Interstate 79 in Franklin Park. Tractors carry visitors into the orchards to pick pumpkins and apples, and roasted corn and apple cider draw crowds to the barn area.

around_teams.latest_developments: Post-Gazette columnist Noah Hiles wrote Friday, September 18, that DK Metcalf has to start playing like the receiver the Steelers pay him to be.
around_teams.summary: Metcalf's first game in a Steelers uniform, the Week 1 win over the Atlanta Falcons, brought drops and penalties, and he told reporters Thursday he is not crying over spilled milk. team_usa.title: Madrid and Barcelona Track Cavan Sullivan
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN's Transfer Talk reported Friday, September 18, that Real Madrid and Barcelona are following Cavan Sullivan, the Philadelphia Union attacker already committed to a future move to Manchester City.
team_usa.summary: Sullivan, 16, got his first senior United States call-up Thursday when manager Mauricio Pochettino named a 28-player roster for the coming FIFA international window. team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN examined Thursday evening, September 17, why Mauricio Pochettino left Christian Pulisic and Folarin Balogun out of his first United States squad since the World Cup.
team_usa.summary: Pulisic, of AC Milan, and Balogun were the leading American attackers at this year's tournament, and both miss the 28-player roster for the September and October FIFA window.
